label: original phase: current and preceding inputs drawn from the r/g/j/t/y/s/3 cluster, early in the sequence
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.9% of mass), never at t=0, the delimiter, or in the copy phase; it peaks at t=2-3 and decays at later positions. The current input has to be one of a token cluster: r is strongest (8x lift, 29% of mass), then g/j/t, then y/u/s/p/3/i. It essentially never fires on b, k or most other letters. It is boosted when the previous inputs (and the one two back) also come from a similar cluster (t/j/g/y/r/s/3/e/v), so it acts like a detector for a run of these tokens near the start. The largest activations are on r right after j/t/r, e.g. y j r. Repeated tokens (in_count>1) also have a somewhat higher rate. Precision is limited: many steps that match the token pattern do not cross the threshold, so this looks like a graded linear readout of recent-input identity rather than a crisp rule. Dev scores: P 0.28, R 0.80, mass recall 0.88.
